Our theory explores the behavior of electron collisions with an ion in a cavity with extremely high electron-wave interaction. In this extremely high coupling regime, electron's spin and wave interactions cause sudden changes that lead to electron and ion bond stabilization through vacuum energy fluctuations. The electron collision rate can be predicted using a modified Breit-Wigner formula, where the width of the quasibound state is influenced by vacuum fluctuations. The cavity's effects can also be observed in the electron scattering pattern, known as forward laser scattering (FLS), which will be investigated in an experimental study. By adjusting the cavity parameters, it may be possible to realize a time scale that is comparable to the electron revolution period around the ion. This could potentially occur within the same period of the driving laser or by using high-speed electron beams. FLS could offer advantages by utilizing lower average cavity photon numbers than traditional Stark spectroscopy, which could lead to increased stability. A comparative investigation of these methods in an experimental setup is recommended. In this investigation, the electron scattering mechanism and the FLS method will be compared to identify the strategies required to optimize each for the measurement of ultrastrong light-matter coupling. The theoretical model we developed is grounded in microphysical principles, which are similar to the principles of the FLS, in contrast to the phenomenological approaches that often prevail in similar light-matter coupling scenarios. Our intention is for this theoretical understanding to provide a foundation for the interpretation of experimental results, without limiting the analysis to specific measurement scenarios. An accompanying supporting information document has been provided to illustrate and explain the underlying numerical results. The code is documented in the corresponding GitHub repository [See Ref. 32]. Furthermore, our investigation challenges the notion that vacuum fluctuations are inherently unstable and show that they can be controlled and harnessed, thus providing valuable insights for future applications in quantum physics and quantum information sciences. This new understanding may also inspire new concepts for quantum-based technologies to manipulate matter in cavities, for instance by introducing negative fluctuations that could potentially realize a quantum clone. In addition to these theoretical findings, our investigation lays the groundwork for the measurement of the light-matter coupling by identifying the crucial parameters of the FLNS method and distinguishing it from other approaches such as the Lamb shift measurements made possible by the HFBS, which involves a broader range of parameters. A more detailed analysis of these other measurement approaches and their parameters, such as the electric dipole coherence and the parametric regime, is however left for another study. In conclusion, our investigation responds to recent calls for more experimental opportunities

In the field of legged locomotion, spring-based elastic actuators can enhance energy efficiency and mobility, but their design and functionality make them distinct from conventional actuators, which may cause issues during training and system integration. This paper introduces a comprehensive framework for modeling and controlling elastic actuators within a whole-system approach, specifically suited for quadruped robots. By developing various actuator designs, researchers are able to train a quadroped robot to navigate using elastic actuators in key movements such as walking and running. Experimental results reveal that elastic actuators can boost energy efficiency by as much as four times over conventional actuators, while maintaining an impressive 98% of conventional peak force production capacity. This innovative work is further demonstrated by an elastic-legged quadruped named Masai which successfully completes a 5 meter hop over 100 times. Analysis indicates that by combining optimal integration and comprehensive model utilization, it is possible to unlock the full potential of spring-based elastic actuators in mobile robotics and related fields. The associated code and models can be accessed at https://github.com/RASLAB/ElasticActuators-for-QuadrupedLocomotion. Video of the research can be viewed at https://youtu.be/m1L4s8D4loE. With successful implementation, spring-based elastic actuators can greatly boost both energy efficiency and mobility in quadruped robots. Furthermore, variations of the designed actuators may have distinct applications such as in human-inspired robots and others in specific fields like rehabilitation and haptic technology. Actual hardware implementation of the designed actuators is planned in the near future. Following conventional optimization strategies may cause a notable decrease in the performance of spring-based elastic actuators in mobile quadruped robots. This paper presents a model that not only enhances our understanding of spring-based elastic actuators but also increases the performance of 12 DoF quadruped robots using elastic actuators in walking and running motions. We propose a new variational quantum algorithm, the Variational Separability Verifier (VSV), to identify the closest N-qubit entangled state that mimics a specific N-qubit Ising symmetry. Our analysis examines the relationship between the quantum circuit depth and the closeness threshold in the context of circuit existence. Additionally, we investigate how different initialization methods and error models affect the threshold, comparing it to an optimal classical algorithm. Our results show that by increasing the circuit depth, VSV enables the generation of closer approximations to entangled states with reduced qubit resources, outperforming a comprehensive list-of-products search. Furthermore, we suggest that exploring the space of mixed states could lead to more efficient solutions of the separability problem. Our findings pave the way for future research on the integration of VSV within variational quantum simulators and quantum development algorithms. It is suggested that in order to study microtearing modes accurately, it is necessary to incorporate electron correlations into the magnetic dynamos. A surge in demand for search by image has led researchers to investigate fashion instance-level image retrieval, which involves finding matching images. Building upon this, the concept of fashion attribute manipulation, which modifies a specific attribute while retaining others, has emerged. This enables users to search not only identical items but also similar items with specific attributes. However, this task is challenging due to the need to preserve a query image's unchanged attributes and retrieve only similar dresses in terms of the target attribute. This paper demonstrates the first approach to manipulate fashion image features. By combining a semi-supervised framework with a pre-trained SSL model, a attribute manipulation model is trained. This consists of two components - a regularisation criterion designed to start learning from limited labelled data, and a two-step training process for the attribute manipulation model. This method requires users to input a query image, a specific attribute, and the feature should be untouched. This results in manipulated images that reflect only changes in desired attributes while retaining others. Experimental trials using a dataset reveal superior retrieval performance of our approach, which outperforms current standards. Due to its underdetermined nature, the method requires an optimal stopping time, for which three rules – a priori choice, the discrepancy principle, and an adapted heuristic principle – are tested in synthetic and real-world scenarios. Constructing the matching cost is a crucial step in estimating light field depth but has received limited attention in the era of deep learning. The prevailing method in the field of deep learning constructs matching cost through the sequential shifting of each sub-aperture image with predefined offsets, making the process intricate and labor-intensive. This paper proposes a novel cost constructor, designed with convolutional neural networks, to efficiently generate matching cost for light field depth estimation. Our constructor leverages pre-defined convolutional neural networks to produce the baseline matching cost and then, through a convolution layer with a unique set of parameters, generates the refined matching cost for each pixel. Furthermore, a key advantage of our proposed constructor is its ability to infers the occlusion map as part of the light field depth estimation process, a feature commonly estimated externally. Our constructor is compatible with various deep learning-based light field depth estimation methods and significantly enhances their performance. Moreover, we introduce a new benchmark, dubbed LF-OC, comprised of twelve 4x3D light field images, to exemplify the capabilities of our constructor in conjunction with state-of-the-art light field depth estimation methods. Our constructor's source code and the LF-OC benchmark are available for public access at https://github.com/ZhangHuihui123/LF-OC. Our findings are published in the journal Image and Vision Computing, where the constructor is first disclosed. Our constructor's performance is showcased in Section 9. This study uses the bilinear method to investigate the Fokas-Lenells equations, first reducing the system and then employing double Wronskian solutions to yield a range of solutions for the reduced equations, resulting in a comprehensive overview of solutions for both classical and nonlocal Fokas-Lenells equations. Several solutions are illustrated through asymptotic analysis, notably, novel solutions are obtained for Fokas-Lenells equations via the Fokas-Rabelo system and the Ablowitz-Ladik system. Furthermore, by means of Bessel functions, a new solution is obtained for the Fokas-Lenells equations in conjunction with the Fokas-Rabelo system. Interestingly, the Fokas-Lenells equations, when combined with the nonlocal Ablowitz-Ladik system, yield solutions exhibiting periodic behavior in combination with an Airy solution, akin to oscillating waves, as well as solutions obtainable from the Fokas-Rabelo system. Moreover, using the knowledge of the wave function of an Schrödinger equation, a new solution is gained for the Fokas-Lenells equations, allowing for asymptotic analysis in certain instances. As a testament to the bilinear method's universality, a range of solutions for the Fokas-Lenells equations, both local and nonlocal variants, have been obtained in this study. Furthermore, by means of the newly discovered solutions, a nonlocal version of the Fokas-Rabelo system is derived, offering a valuable contribution to the existing body of knowledge on the subject. Finally, we choose an Airy solution of the Fokas-Lenells equations, both local and nonlocal variants, such that the energy remains constant over time and the momentum reverses direction. In conclusion, the systems have achieved a complete overview of solutions for both local and nonlocal variants. This research constructs actions for alternative gravity theories within the context of double field theory. By doing so, it uncovers a link between the gravity theories and frame rotations, resulting in novel, non-Riemannian gravity actions that incorporate a branch cut. To meet growing demands for next-generation home WiFi networks, it is essential to improve their performance capabilities. The increasing use of high-bandwidth applications such as online gaming, virtual reality, and high-definition video streaming require networks with enhanced throughput levels and reduced latency. One effective strategy for enhancing WiFi network performance in dense environments, such as metropolitan areas and large homes, involves deploying mesh networks, which can achieve this by automatically switching between mesh and bridge configurations to optimize performance. However, achieving quality of service (QoS) in such networks poses a challenge, particularly when integrating existing networks with new devices and features without affecting Q related metrics. To address this issue, we developed a channel load-aware AP/Extender selection mechanism that leverages the IEEE 802.11k/v standard to optimize performance in mesh networks. Our mechanism involves two primary modules that respectively identify resources and allocate resources within the network. Through simulations, we demonstrated that our mechanism can achieve a 90% similarity score with a time complexity of O(nf) and an efficient resource allocation value of 70%. The practical feasibility of our proposal was also validated through a successful trial deployment at a US-based telecom provider. Moreover, we successfully integrated our mechanism with the Mesh networking in Linux Kernel 5.11, achieving a high degree of practicality. The contribution of our research enables developers to enhance the performance of mesh networks and integrates well with existing standards such as IEEE 802.11k/v and IEEE 802.11. Our source code for the trial deployment is publicly available on GitHub. This research contributes towards developing QoS-aware AP/Extender selection and coexistence techniques that can enhance the performance of bridge networks. The mechanism is adaptable to various bridge configurations, including star and mesh topologies, and recommends the most suitable AP/Extender based on parameters such as return delay, bandwidth, and time. Our simulation results demonstrate the efficacy of our mechanism in outperforming other existing methods. Ultimately, we successfully demonstrated that our mechanism can coexist with IEEE 802.11k/v, thereby validating its practicality. The trial deployment of our mechanism at a US-based telecom provider, as well as the integration of our codebase with the Mesh networking in Linux Kernel 5.11, affirms the high degree of development efficacy.
